subject: general
question: The median of a set of 7 distinct observations is 21.5. If each of the largest 3 observations of the set is increased by 4, then the median of the new set -

options.text: will remain the same as that of the original set
will be four times the original median

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a set of **n = 7** observations, the **median** is the **4th** term when arranged in ascending order.

Increasing the **largest 3 observations** (the 5th, 6th, and 7th terms) does not affect the value or position of the **4th term**.

Since the **middle term** remains unchanged, the **median** remains the same.

**∴ The correct answer is will remain the same as that of the original set.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of observations (n) = 7 (**odd**)

Original Median = 21.5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f566f42e46094a85493ab7a1547c4cb96ca6a17e224fa1e5ff27b45de4447248.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the observations in ascending order be x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄, x₅, x₆, x₇.

⇒ Median for odd n = [(n + 1)/2]th observation.

⇒ Median = [(7 + 1)/2]th observation = 4th observation.

⇒ 4th observation (x₄) = 21.5.

⇒ The largest 3 observations are x₅, x₆, and x₇.

⇒ After increasing x₅, x₆, and x₇ by 4, the new set becomes x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄, (x₅+4), (x₆+4), (x₇+4).

⇒ Since x₄ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If n is even, the median is the **average** of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th observations.

Robustness of Median

The **median** is a measure of **central tendency** that is not affected by **extreme values** (outliers) as long as the relative order of the middle elements is unchanged.

Linear Transformation Rule

If **every** observation in a set is increased by a constant k, the median also **increases by k**. However, changing only a subset of values may not affect the median.</p
